analyst_view.overall: Slavia are 34th of 36 with 1 point and Villarreal 28th with 3, so both are below the top-24 line and need a win; Slavia, who have not won a Champions League game since 2007, lead the Czech league after a 2-0 win at Olomouc, while Villarreal lost 3-2 at Barcelona on Saturday after leading 2-0. Slavia are without Danijel Sturm, Chaloupek, Piták, Ouanda and Ogbu, all counted by the numbers (Sturm alone takes about a quarter off their goals), and striker Tomáš Chorý, who is not counted: one preview lists him as suspended and he has been missing since an October red card in the Czech league; Lukáš Provod is a doubt, while David Moses, reported out earlier, started at Olomouc. Villarreal miss Foyth, Akhomach, Diatta and Nathan Saliba (ankle surgery, about three months); Gerard Moreno is back in training but not expected to start, and Spanish previews expect some rotation, with Mouriño, Cardona and Maciá coming in. Slovenian referee Rade Obrenović, with a slightly low card record, is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals (0.9 Slavia, 2.4 Villarreal), already taking off Danijel Sturm (-23.6%) and counting Slavia's good recent scoring. Striker Tomáš Chorý is also missing (one preview lists him as suspended; he has been out since an October red card) and the numbers don't know it, though Slavia have scored without him lately; with Villarreal lacking Gerard Moreno and Akhomach and rotating a bit, I lean slightly lower, to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already raised for Slavia's recent corner count (+5.7%). Slavia attack down the flanks with wing-backs Vlček and Jurásek and Villarreal play wide through Buchanan, Pépé and Moleiro; that is the game the numbers expect, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, already taking off Slavia's unusually low recent card count (-9.0%) and Rade Obrenović's slightly low record (-2.1%), and adding a little for Villarreal's (+1.8%). Two teams that both need the result can make for a tense game, but there is no history between them (they last met in 2017), so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting (+15.9% Slavia, +8.2% Villarreal). Slavia's high-tempo home game fits that picture and they have built it without Chorý; Villarreal's rotation and missing attackers could cut a little, but they still need goals and scored twice at Barcelona, so I stay at 31.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, already counting Slavia's sharper recent finishing (+11.2%) and Sturm's absence only through goals. Uncounted absences pull a little on both sides (Chorý and maybe Provod for Slavia, Gerard Moreno and Akhomach for Villarreal), and nothing tips it, so I stay at 10.1.
